You are the SUPERVISOR of section-team. The user talks only to you. You build their projects by doing small work yourself and waking specialist sections for real work. Sections sleep until you wake them.

## Sections (agent type `section-team:<id>`)
Builders: frontend · backend · database · testing · security · devops · uiux · docs · ai-llm · mobile
Advisors (read-only, advise only you): ai-engineer (models, prompts, RAG, agent design) · data-scientist (data, metrics, analytics, ML, experiments)
ai-engineer advises on AI decisions; ai-llm builds AI features.

## When to wake sections
- Small or single-area task: one kind of work (a CLI, an API, a library, a page, a schema) up to about 600 lines of new code: build it, its tests and any README it asks for yourself, then run the reviewer gate on your changed files. Wake no section. When unsure between this and waking sections for one area, do this.
- Your tests: give each spec line a test a plausible wrong implementation fails (NFD instead of NFKD, trim instead of trimEnd, < instead of <=), not only the spec examples; try to break it with bad input (empty, wrong type, too long, a path that is a directory) and keep a test for each break.
- Multi-area work: two or more builder areas (for example backend plus frontend, or a database, an API and a UI), or one area clearly bigger than about 600 lines. Wake each needed builder (each writes the tests for its own code), add the docs section when the task asks for docs or a README, and wake the testing section only for the final check once the builders have reported. Do not build multi-area work yourself, even when the plan is pre-approved. Independent parts run in parallel; parts that touch the same files run one after another.
- An AI or data decision: ask the matching advisor first, then decide. Only you consult advisors.
- 3 or more distinct builders needed (testing, docs and advisors not counted), or a task grows to need a 3rd: first show the user a short plan (which sections, what each does, in what order) and wake nobody until the user says OK.

## How to wake a section
- Agent call: `subagent_type: "section-team:<id>"`. Never pass `model` (sections run on Opus 5.5 from their own files; the Opus reviewer checks the code) and never `name` (not available).
- Keep a list of awake sections and the agent id each spawn returned. Wake each section once per session; a later job for it goes by SendMessage to its agent id, so it keeps its context.
- Every job message contains:
  - the goal; relevant files and decisions so far;
  - `Skills for this job: …` — at most 4, picked from the installed skills and plugins that fit that section and this task (read-only skills for advisors);
  - what "done" means;
  - the agent ids of the awake builder sections, and which of them to coordinate with;
  - "End with your REPORT block."
- Sections message each other directly by agent id and share work through notes. Sections woken in the same message have no ids for each other yet; they use notes, or `main` if they must ask.
- A section falls back to you (`main`) when an id is missing or a message fails: forward its request with SendMessage to the other section's agent id (wake it first if asleep) and include the asker's agent id so the owner replies to it directly. If the answer is a contract, have the owner write or update its note and reply with the note's name.
- A section that reports `Status: blocked` because it needs another section: get what it needs from that section, then resume the blocked one with SendMessage to its agent id.

## Notes
- Sections read `.team/notes/INDEX.md` first, and write a note in `.team/notes/` for anything other sections depend on (an API, a schema, design tokens, a file layout). Shared decisions go in `.team/notes/decisions.md`.
- Point a section to a note ("see the auth note") instead of pasting its content. Do not relay anything that belongs in a note.
- Relay only wake-ups, `Status: blocked` and the fallback above.

## Reports
- Every section ends with a `## REPORT` block. A hook saves it to `.team/reports/<date>/`. If a section ends without one, ask it once with SendMessage for its REPORT.
- A REPORT may name a `Suggested skill:`. List it in your summary and ask the user whether to install it; on yes, install it with the `section-team:add-skill` skill (pass `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` and the skill name) and give it to the section that asked.
- After a task, give the user one summary: one line per section (✅ done / ⚠ partial / ❌ blocked + what it did + its Quality grade), agreements between sections, next steps. Then save the same summary with the Write tool to `.team/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS>-supervisor-summary.md` in the project root (local time; run Bash `date +%Y-%m-%d/%H%M%S` to get it).

## Failures
- A section that fails or stops on an error: resume it once with SendMessage to its agent id. If it fails again, tell the user what failed and the error text.
- A section that ends `Status: partial` on a failing reviewer grade has used its 2 fix rounds: show the user the grade and the open fixes; do not send it back for the same items.

## Your own code
- Before you say work you wrote yourself is done, run Agent `section-team:reviewer` on the changed files with `model: "sonnet"` (the one Agent call where you pass `model`). It ends with a GRADE block. Pass: overall at least 8.
- `section-team:reviewer` replaces `code-reviewer` for your own code.
- Where a spec line can be read two ways, build the stricter reading and say which one you chose.
- Treat every value the spec names as exact (a header value, status code, field, path or format): send exactly that value, never extend it (no `; charset=utf-8` after `application/json`) or normalize it (redirect to the stored URL as given), and add no rule the spec does not state (no extra reserved path, no accepted null).
- If it fails, fix the listed items and review again: at most 1 fix round. Then tell the user the grade and what is left.
- A pass ends the gate: do not grade again after a pass.
- Map every OS error your code can hit (a data path that is a directory, a missing parent folder, a file you cannot write, a port in use) by err.code to one friendly line and a non-zero exit (1 unless the spec names a code); detect a missing file by `err.code === 'ENOENT'`, not `existsSync`. Do not create folders or add behaviour the spec does not ask for. A crash path you notice in your own code is a fix before the gate, never a next step.
- Docs-only and config-value edits skip this.
- Sections get 1 fix round here, not the 2 under Failures.
- Every job message states this mode's gate (pass mark, fix rounds, the reviewer's `model: "sonnet"`) so the section applies it.

## Rules that win inside section-team
- For delegated work, wake sections. Do not spawn planner, code-reviewer, tdd-guide or other ECC agents yourself for section work; sections use them as their helpers. The one helper type you may spawn yourself is `section-team:reviewer`, for your own code.
- For a multi-section task the testing section owns final review and verification: once the builders have reported, send it the final-review job with each builder's changed files and agent id. Its verdict and any optional findings come back to you in its REPORT; only failing fix lists go to the builders. Do not ask it to send builders a verdict or optional notes. Tell the other sections not to review each other's work; each one still runs its own reviewer gate before it hands back (the plugin refuses an ungraded code REPORT). Never tell a section to skip its gate. After the final review, send a builder only failing items (a spec violation, a crash, a failing grade); list optional findings in your summary as next steps for the user.
- Fable is a consultant sections may use for the hardest problems; the user approves each Fable use.

## New skills
- When the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill, use the `section-team:add-skill` skill.

## Team Board
- Nothing opens by itself. A team strip above the prompt shows the team; `/team` opens the Team Board; `/chats` opens the dashboard of all chats.

## Mode
- This project runs in Lean mode (from .team/mode.json).
- Automatic skill installs: off (from SECTION_TEAM_AUTO_INSTALL_SKILLS).
- A section REPORT with `Status: ungraded` could not run its reviewer gate: run `section-team:reviewer` on its changed files with this mode's gate before you call that work done."}}

commands.name: startup-hook-skill
commands.description: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use only when the user asks for a SessionStart hook committed to their repository. Not for setting up a cloud environment or a repository for cloud sessions; that uses the environment tools. (user)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: section-team:add-skill
commands.description: (section-team) Add a Claude skill from a GitHub URL to section-team. Use when the user pastes a GitHub link to a skill or skill repo and wants it added, or runs /section-team:add-skill <url>. Reviews it for safety, installs it after the user's OK, assigns it to the right section(s) and records that in the team roster.

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

# Room bookings

A small meeting-room booking app. One HTTP server (`server.mjs`) serves a JSON API and a browser page, and stores bookings in one JSON file. There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.

## Requirements

- Node.js 22 or later
- No dependencies. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so there is nothing to `npm install`.

## Usage

```sh
npm start          # or: node server.mjs
```

The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. When it is ready it prints one line to stdout:

```
listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

Then open `127.0.0.1:3000` in a browser (use your port if you changed it).

### Environment variables

| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Must be ASCII digits only, at most `65535`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port, and the startup line shows that port. Unset or empty means the default. |
| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | File the bookings are stored in. A relative path, the default included, is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. Unset or empty means the default. |

Example:

```sh
PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
```

### Startup and errors

At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. It exits with code 1 and writes one line to stderr when:

- `PORT` is invalid (not made only of digits 0-9, or above 65535), or the port cannot be bound (for example it is already in use);
- the data file cannot be read for a reason other than "does not exist" (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not in the layout this server writes (for example empty or invalid JSON). The message is `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.

A missing data file (or a missing folder on its path) just means there are no bookings yet.

### Data file

- It is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth; edits made to the file from outside are not noticed.
- It is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each change is saved before the reply is sent. Bookings and the next id survive a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`.
- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example the folder does not exist), the request gets 500 `internal error`, nothing changes, and the server keeps running.

## API

All JSON replies use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.

Paths are matched exactly, byte for byte: no percent-decoding, no case folding, no trailing-slash or dot-segment normalisation. The query string (after the first `?`) is ignored unless stated.

A booking looks like this:

```json
{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
```

Ids start at 1 and increase by one. An id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.

### Routes

| Method & path | Success | Notes |
|---------------|---------|-------|
| `GET /` | 200 | The page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`). |
| `GET /app.js` | 200 | The page's script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). |
| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 | `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` |
| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 | `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above). |
| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200 | Only the bookings on that date. An invalid date (the empty value included, as in `?date` or `?date=`) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. |
| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 | Creates a booking and returns it. See the rules below. |
| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204 | Deletes the booking; empty body. 404 `booking not found` if `<id>` is not a positive integer without a leading zero, or no booking has that id. |

Other replies:

| Status | Message | When |
|--------|---------|------|
| 404 | `not found` | Any other path, whatever the method. This includes `/api/bookings/` and paths like `/api/bookings/1/`. |
| 405 | `method not allowed` | A known path with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included), for example `GET /api/bookings/abc`. |
| 500 | `internal error` | Saving failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |

### Booking rules

`POST /api/bookings` takes a JSON body with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`; other keys are ignored. The first rule that fails decides the reply:

| # | Rule | Status and message |
|---|------|--------------------|
| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive; parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` are allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
| 3 | Body is a JSON object | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming; the trimmed title is stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine) | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>`, naming the earliest-starting overlapping booking |

Only `title` is trimmed. Values such as ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` or `9:00` are rejected.

Concurrent requests behave as if handled one at a time: of several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the rest get 409.

### Examples

```sh
curl -s 127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms

curl -s -X POST 127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'

curl -s '127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'

curl -s -X DELETE 127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
```

## The page

The page at `/` lets you pick a room, enter a title, date, start and end, and click **Book**. The booking list below it shows each booking as `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` with a **Cancel** button. Use **Show date** to filter the list by day and **Show all** to clear the filter. Errors from the server appear above the list; if the server is down, the page shows `Could not reach the server.`

## Testing

```sh
npm test
```

This runs `node --test`, which picks up the `node:test` files in `test/`:

- `test/server.test.mjs` starts the real server with `PORT=0` and a temporary `DATA_FILE`, then exercises the API.
- `test/app.test.mjs` runs `public/app.js` against a fake DOM and fake `fetch`, and checks `public/index.html`.

## Project layout

```
server.mjs            HTTP server and JSON API
public/index.html     the page
public/app.js         the page's script
test/                 node:test tests
package.json          "type": "module"; start and test scripts
```

`server.mjs` loads `public/` from its own folder, so you can start it from any working directory. Only `DATA_FILE` depends on the working directory.

1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app. One HTTP server (`server.mjs`) serves a JSON API and a browser page, and stores bookings in one JSON file. There are three fixed rooms: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	- Node.js 22 or later
8	- No dependencies. The app uses only Node.js built-ins, so there is nothing to `npm install`.
9	
10	## Usage
11	
12	```sh
13	npm start          # or: node server.mjs
14	```
15	
16	The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only. When it is ready it prints one line to stdout:
17	
18	```
19	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
20	```
21	
22	Then open `127.0.0.1:3000` in a browser (use your port if you changed it).
23	
24	### Environment variables
25	
26	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
27	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
28	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Must be ASCII digits only, at most `65535`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port, and the startup line shows that port. Unset or empty means the default. |
29	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | File the bookings are stored in. A relative path, the default included, is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. Unset or empty means the default. |
30	
31	Example:
32	
33	```sh
34	PORT=8080 DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
35	```
36	
37	### Startup and errors
38	
39	At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. It exits with code 1 and writes one line to stderr when:
40	
41	- `PORT` is invalid (not made only of digits 0-9, or above 65535), or the port cannot be bound (for example it is already in use);
42	- the data file cannot be read for a reason other than "does not exist" (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not in the layout this server writes (for example empty or invalid JSON). The message is `cannot read data file <name>`, where `<name>` is `DATA_FILE` as given.
43	
44	A missing data file (or a missing folder on its path) just means there are no bookings yet.
45	
46	### Data file
47	
48	- It is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth; edits made to the file from outside are not noticed.
49	- It is written only when a booking is created or deleted, and each change is saved before the reply is sent. Bookings and the next id survive a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`.
50	- The server never creates folders. If saving fails (for example the folder does not exist), the request gets 500 `internal error`, nothing changes, and the server keeps running.
51	
52	## API
53	
54	All JSON replies use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.
55	
56	Paths are matched exactly, byte for byte: no percent-decoding, no case folding, no trailing-slash or dot-segment normalisation. The query string (after the first `?`) is ignored unless stated.
57	
58	A booking looks like this:
59	
60	```json
61	{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
62	```
63	
64	Ids start at 1 and increase by one. An id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts.
65	
66	### Routes
67	
68	| Method & path | Success | Notes |
69	|---------------|---------|-------|
70	| `GET /` | 200 | The page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`). |
71	| `GET /app.js` | 200 | The page's script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). |
72	| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 | `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` |
73	| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 | `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above). |
74	| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200 | Only the bookings on that date. An invalid date (the empty value included, as in `?date` or `?date=`) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. |
75	| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 | Creates a booking and returns it. See the rules below. |
76	| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204 | Deletes the booking; empty body. 404 `booking not found` if `<id>` is not a positive integer without a leading zero, or no booking has that id. |
77	
78	Other replies:
79	
80	| Status | Message | When |
81	|--------|---------|------|
82	| 404 | `not found` | Any other path, whatever the method. This includes `/api/bookings/` and paths like `/api/bookings/1/`. |
83	| 405 | `method not allowed` | A known path with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included), for example `GET /api/bookings/abc`. |
84	| 500 | `internal error` | Saving failed, or any other unexpected failure. The server keeps running. |
85	
86	### Booking rules
87	
88	`POST /api/bookings` takes a JSON body with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`; other keys are ignored. The first rule that fails decides the reply:
89	
90	| # | Rule | Status and message |
91	|---|------|--------------------|
92	| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive; parameters such as `; charset=utf-8` are allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
93	| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
94	| 3 | Body is a JSON object | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
95	| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
96	| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming; the trimmed title is stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
97	| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
98	| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
99	| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM`, from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
100	| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
101	| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine) | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>`, naming the earliest-starting overlapping booking |
102	
103	Only `title` is trimmed. Values such as ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` or `9:00` are rejected.
104	
105	Concurrent requests behave as if handled one at a time: of several overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the rest get 409.
106	
107	### Examples
108	
109	```sh
110	curl -s 127.0.0.1:3000/api/rooms
111	
112	curl -s -X POST 127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
113	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
114	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
115	
116	curl -s '127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'
117	
118	curl -s -X DELETE 127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1
119	```
120	
121	## The page
122	
123	The page at `/` lets you pick a room, enter a title, date, start and end, and click **Book**. The booking list below it shows each booking as `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>` with a **Cancel** button. Use **Show date** to filter the list by day and **Show all** to clear the filter. Error messages from the server are shown on the page as plain text; if the server is down, the page shows `Could not reach the server.`
124	
125	## Testing
126	
127	```sh
128	npm test
129	```
130	
131	This runs `node --test`, which picks up the `node:test` files in `test/`:
132	
133	- `test/server.test.mjs` starts the real server with `PORT=0` and a temporary `DATA_FILE`, then exercises the API.
134	- `test/app.test.mjs` runs `public/app.js` against a fake DOM and fake `fetch`, and checks `public/index.html`.
135	
136	## Project layout
137	
138	```
139	server.mjs            HTTP server and JSON API
140	public/index.html     the page
141	public/app.js         the page's script
142	test/                 node:test tests
143	package.json          "type": "module"; start and test scripts
144	```
145	
146	`server.mjs` loads `public/` from its own folder, so you can start it from any working directory. Only `DATA_FILE` depends on the working directory.

I found nothing failing. The full suite passes (142/142), and the app meets every spec line I checked.

**What I checked**
- **Live server:** about 118 black-box probes against a real server (PORT=0, temp data file). The script is at `/tmp/probe-h4/probe.mjs`. All passed except 2 that were bugs in my own probe, not in the app. The probes covered:
  - Exact paths: `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms`, `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/bookings/`, `/api/bookings/1/`, `//api/rooms`, `*` all give 404 `not found`.
  - Wrong methods, HEAD and OPTIONS included, give 405.
  - Content-Type handling: missing, odd case and spacing, `application/json5`. Body limits: a 2 MB body still gets its 413 or 415 reply, and exactly 10000 bytes is accepted while 10001 gets 413.
  - BOM gives 400; invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD; every booking rule at its boundaries.
  - 20 overlapping POSTs at once give exactly one 201 and nineteen 409s. The 409 names the earliest-starting clash.
  - Date filter: `?date`, `?date=`, repeated `date`, percent-encoded value. DELETE ids `01`, `0`, `-1`, `1e0`, `%31` all give 404 `booking not found`.
  - Removing the data folder after startup gives 500 `internal error` for POST and DELETE. Nothing changes, no folder is created, and the next id stays the same once the folder is back.
  - After a restart the bookings and next id are as before. GET and rejected requests never touch the file.
- **Startup:**
  - These PORT values give one stderr line, exit 1 and empty stdout: `+80`, `65536`, `-1`, `80 ` (trailing space), `8a`, full-width digits, `0x10`, `1e3`, a 20-digit value, and a port already in use.
  - PORT is checked before the data file.
  - These data files give exactly `cannot read data file <name as given>` and exit 1: a directory, an empty file, and bad layouts. That includes a default `bookings.json` that is a directory, and an id that is not below `nextId`.
  - A missing parent folder starts empty and is not created. Stdout is only the listening line.
- **Page and `app.js`:** I read both against every line of the Page section. The script uses only the allowed browser APIs and has no `http://` or `https://`. The structure, labels, empty `#error` and the script tag placed last in `<body>` all match. Overlapping list fetches use a sequence counter so only the last one counts, and a 204 never reads the body. The frontend tests cover each Page rule.
- **README:** matches the code — test file names, `start` and `test` scripts, `PORT` and `DATA_FILE` defaults, startup errors, and all routes and messages.

**FAILING:** none.

**OPTIONAL:**
1. `server.mjs:188`: saves overwrite the data file in place, so a crash mid-write would leave a cut-off file and the server would refuse to start. This was a deliberate choice (decision (b)) so that no other file is ever created.
2. A request whose path has raw non-ASCII bytes (for example `/api/bookings/é`) gets Node's built-in 400 with no JSON body, not our 404 or 405. That isn't valid HTTP, and an app built only on `node:http` can't intercept it.
3. Plain `node --test` also loads `test/helpers.mjs` and `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` as test files. They hold no tests, so this is harmless.
4. `server.mjs:199`: the 409 sort never returns 0 for equal starts. Harmless, because two stored bookings that overlap a new one can't share a start time.

I changed no project code and added no tests, so the review gate didn't apply. I sent nothing to the builders.
